Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Tazmin Brits and Lara Goodall are the two openers for the South Africa Women. Sneh Rana has the new ball in hand. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

South African women were decent with the ball in the first powerplay and took crucial wickets, but found it hard to contain the Indian batting through the middle and the tail end of the innings. Masabata Klaas, Nadine De Klerk, and Nonkululeko Mlaba snapped two wickets each but were on the expensive side, while Chloe Tryon and Annerie Dercksen took one apiece. The Proteas Women will need to bat out of their skin if they are to breach the total set by India Women. They are also without their regular skipper and star batter, Laura Wolvaardt, and the challenge will be tougher under trying conditions. Join us in a while for South Africa Women's reply.

A solid batting effort from the India Women helps them post a substantial score of 337/9 from their 50 overs. Having been sent into bat first, India Women lost three wickets inside the first seven overs, but Smriti Mandhana and Jemimah Rodrigues added an 88-run stand to steady the ship and set a strong base. Mandhana was dismissed after getting her fifty, but Rodrigues carried on and smashed an outstanding hundred for her side. Deepti Sharma provided good support to Jemimah Rodrigues initially and took on the bowlers post her dismissal. Deepti Sharma ended with 93 off 84 balls, and cameos from Richa Ghosh and Shree Charani took the score past the 330-run mark.

OUT! RUN OUT! Sneh Rana is short at the bowling end! A fuller delivery outside the off stump. Rana steps outside the crease and hits it down the ground. The fielder at long off estimates it's wide and chases after the ball. The batters decide to run for two, but the throw from long off reaches the bowling end. Charani struggles to make her ground, and Nadine De Klerk collects the ball and dislodges the bails. India Women end their innings at 337/9!
